NavigationOut.description:
One committed main-frame document.

``index`` is the public identifier of a navigation and is what every filter
takes. ``chain_index`` groups the hops of one HTTP redirect chain, so a
client can collapse ``a?id=1 -> www.a -> google`` into one row when it
wants the summary and expand it when it wants the hops.
NavigationOut.title: NavigationOut

NavigationTrigger.description:
What moved the browser into a navigation.

Taken from Chromium itself, through the CDP event
``Page.frameRequestedNavigation``, so unlike a hook in the page realm it
cannot be defeated by the page. ``UNKNOWN`` means the browser gave no
reason, never that nothing happened.
NavigationTrigger.title: NavigationTrigger

PayloadOut.description:
One file the target delivered to the browser.

``kind`` is the only field that describes the content. ``filename``,
``declared_mime``, and ``content_disposition`` are claims by the analysed
page, so ``filename_source`` records where the name came from.

``digests_identify_file`` is false for a truncated record. The digests
then describe the recorded bytes only, so they must not be used to look
up the delivered file in an external source.
PayloadOut.title: PayloadOut

RequestAttribution.description:
How confidently a request was tied to a navigation.

``EXACT`` means the browser named the frame that issued it. ``INFERRED``
means it was placed by start time against the navigation boundaries, which is
a guess. ``NONE`` means neither was possible, which is the honest answer
for a pre-migration analysis and for most of a replayed one.

An assurance signal reports evidence that an operator must pay for or pass
a check to obtain. Severity states the magnitude, not the polarity, so an
assurance signal at MEDIUM subtracts what a risk signal at MEDIUM adds.
